answer: Co-residency interference probes: at random moments the network gives one key a heavy memory-thrashing job while timing a tiny job on another randomly chosen key. Agents on separate machines never notice, but keys packed onto one host slow down in lockstep, their shared caches cracking like crystal under load. Pairs that keep stalling together are merged into one reward slot, so a grove of sybils grown on one server earns like a single agent, while honest agents feel only a velvet-soft delay.
